dispositions.topic_text: Persistence and uniqueness semantics for Registry-to-Kernel request-id trace correlation
dispositions.reason: R0-92 assigns whether Kernel writes the request id into its trace record, and so persistence and uniqueness of the correlation, to the cabinet-kernel case (matrix K1); Registry already keeps the request id of a room's create and a pointer's publish (M03, M05, A01) and this decision adds no fact or rule to Registry.

dispositions.topic_text: Whether legacy objects-folder cleanup must precede production start and import
dispositions.what: R0-98's screening conclusion holds once the owner's earlier machine no longer gives the agent the objects folder (home-server move, step 7). Deployment must verify, before the screening's conclusion is recorded, that the agent's user cannot read the objects folder on the home server (sudo -u cabinet-agent ls /srv/cabinet refused) and that the agent no longer runs as a user who reads the old ~/Загрузки/работа on the owner's machine. Registry's production start and its one import (R0-79) do not wait for this: they lower the risk.
keeps:
Photos of the objects — homes — do not reach the
agent either: on the home server the objects folder belongs to the `cabinet`
user and the agent's user cannot read it (Factory
`platform/home_server/README.md`), and Kernel moves a file between services
through its run's spool without ever handing it to a caller (case
`cabinet-kernel`, K-10); the agent names a photo for Client Portal, it never
sees one.
options: Verify cleanup before production start and import.
Permit production first but disable agent operation until cleanup is verified.
Permit production and import while the old folder remains reachable.
consequences: The first directly preserves the photo-isolation claim.
The second requires an independently enforced deployment gate.
The third admits an exposure interval and cannot preserve the quoted guarantee.
